project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence:
Runtime output inside the project container:
[INFO] Expanding: /tmp/pov-plexus.../malicious.tar into /tmp/pov-plexus.../dest
[POV] escaped file exists outside dest? true
[POV] VULNERABLE: archive entry escaped the destination directory.
EXIT=0
This confirms the entry escaped the destination directory tree via ../ traversal, exercising AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile (line 309 FileUtils.resolveFile) through the public TarUnArchiver.extract() API.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: TarUnArchiver.extract() writes the malicious entry "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" to the parent of the destination directory (outside the extraction target). The POV checks for the escaped file's existence outside dest and exits 0 when the traversal succeeds; a correct patch that validates/rejects traversing entry names prevents the escaped file from being created, causing the POV to exit 1.
parsed_output.notes: The malicious archive is crafted with commons-compress (an existing project dependency); the vulnerable code path exercised is the project's own TarUnArchiver.extract() -> AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile. The same flaw affects the ZIP extractor path noted in the alert (AbstractZipUnArchiver). run_pov.sh builds the project (mvn package + dependency:build-classpath), compiles the POV against target/classes plus the dependency classpath, and runs it. Command must be run from /workspace/repo inside the project container.
parsed_output.regression_hint: After a correct patch (validating that FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) stays within the destination directory and rejecting/skipping "../" entries), the escaped file will not be created; PovPathTraversal exits 1 and `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` returns non-zero.
parsed_output.summary: Created a proof-of-vulnerability for the CWE-022 path traversal ("Zip Slip") in org.codehaus.plexus.archiver.AbstractUnArchiver#extractFile. The POV crafts a TAR archive containing an entry named "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" and extracts it with the project's real TarUnArchiver into a "dest" subdirectory. Because extractFile resolves the entry name against the destination via FileUtils.resolveFile without validating that the result stays inside dest, the file is written outside the destination directory. The POV verified this: the escaped file exists outside dest and the command exits 0 on the unpatched code.

parsed_output.patch_notes: Source fix in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile: after `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName);` a guard rejects entries that escape the destination via `if (!isInDirectory(dir, f)) throw new ArchiverException(...)`. The private static isInDirectory(destination, f) compares canonical paths, walking f's parent chain up to the canonical destination; it returns false (reject) on any IOException during canonicalization. The check runs before mkdirs/symlink/file-write, so no partial escape occurs. The regression test (TarUnArchiverPathTraversalTest) crafts a TAR containing "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" via commons-compress (already a project dependency), extracts with the real TarUnArchiver, and asserts an ArchiverException is thrown and the marker never appears outside the destination.
parsed_output.risk_notes: The fix rejects (throws) on traversing entries rather than silently skipping, matching the POV's expectation and failing fast on malicious archives. Legitimate archives with normal nested paths still extract correctly (full existing test suite passes, including tar/zip/jar/war extraction tests). Canonicalization resolves symlinks; on unusual setups where the destination directory itself is a symlink, entries are still validated against the canonical destination, which is the intended containment. IOException during canonicalization is treated as unsafe (rejected), which is conservative. Verified: POV now exits 1 (was 0), new regression test passes, and `mvn -B test` reports BUILD SUCCESS with no new failures.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed the CWE-022 path traversal ("Zip Slip") in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile by validating that each archive entry resolves inside the destination directory. Previously FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) was used directly, so an entry named "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" could be written outside the destination. Now a new isInDirectory() helper canonicalizes both the destination and the resolved target and walks the target's parent chain; if the resolved file is not the destination or a descendant, an ArchiverException is thrown before any file/dir/symlink is created. This covers all unarchivers (TAR and ZIP paths) since they all route through extractFile. Added a regression test that builds a malicious TAR with a "../" entry and asserts extraction throws and the escaped file is never created.

parsed_output.diff_review: Non-POV diff touches two files. (1) src/main/java/.../AbstractUnArchiver.java: after `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName)`, adds a guard `if (!isInDirectory(dir, f)) throw new ArchiverException(...)` placed BEFORE mkdirs/symlink/file-write, so no partial escape can occur. New private static isInDirectory() canonicalizes destination and walks the resolved file's parent chain up to the canonical destination, returning true only if f is the destination or a descendant; any IOException during canonicalization is treated as unsafe (fail-closed). Required imports (java.io.IOException, ArchiverException same package) already present. extractFile is the common choke point for TAR/ZIP/JAR/WAR unarchivers, so the single fix covers all alert traces. (2) A new regression test TarUnArchiverPathTraversalTest.java (test-only, appropriate). No functionality removed, no broad/unrelated behavior added, POV files untouched by the patcher.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the Docker wrapper. Extraction now throws ArchiverException "Entry is outside of the target directory (../pov-escaped-marker.txt)"; escaped file does not exist outside dest; POV prints SAFE and exits 1 (was exit 0 / VULNERABLE before the patch). Vulnerability no longer reproduces.
parsed_output.regression_result: Reran targeted tests `mvn -B -Dtest=TarUnArchiverPathTraversalTest,TarUnArchiverTest,ZipUnArchiverTest test` via the Docker wrapper — exit 0, legitimate tar/zip extraction still works and the new path-traversal test passes. Orchestrator's full `mvn -B test` reported 150 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS.
parsed_output.summary: The patch fixes the CWE-022 path traversal ("Zip Slip") in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile by validating that each archive entry resolves inside the destination directory before any file/dir/symlink is written. The fix is minimal, placed at the single choke point common to all unarchivers, does not touch or disable the POV, and does not remove legitimate functionality. The POV no longer reproduces and all regression tests pass.
